topicName: SQL Data Types: Numeric, String, Date/Time
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"SQL Data Types: Numeric, String, Date/Time"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"SQL data types specify the type of data that a column can hold. Choosing the correct data type is crucial for data integrity, storage efficiency, and query performance. This tutorial covers the fundamental SQL data types: Numeric, String, and Date/Time."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Numeric Data Types"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Numeric data types are used to store numerical values. SQL offers several numeric types with varying precision and range."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Integer Types"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Integer types store whole numbers (numbers without decimal points)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"INT or INTEGER: A standard integer type. The range typically varies depending on the database system, but it's commonly -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SMALLINT: A smaller integer type, offering a smaller range, typically -32,768 to 32,767. Uses less storage than INT."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"TINYINT: The smallest integer type, with a range typically from 0 to 255 (unsigned) or -128 to 127 (signed). Uses the least storage."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"BIGINT: A large integer type, with a much larger range than INT, typically -9,223,372,036,854,775,808 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE employees (
    employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    age TINYINT,
    salary INT
);"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Floating-Point Types"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Floating-point types store numbers with decimal points."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"FLOAT: A single-precision floating-point number."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DOUBLE or DOUBLE PRECISION: A double-precision floating-point number, offering greater precision than FLOAT."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"REAL: Another floating-point type, often synonymous with FLOAT or DOUBLE depending on the database system."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    price FLOAT,
    weight DOUBLE PRECISION
);"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Fixed-Point Types"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Fixed-point types store numbers with a fixed number of decimal places, providing exact precision."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DECIMAL(p, s) or NUMERIC(p, s): Stores exact numeric values. 'p' is the precision (total number of digits), and 's' is the scale (number of digits to the right of the decimal point)."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    total_amount DECIMAL(10, 2)
);"},{"order":22,"type":"heading","text":"String Data Types"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"String data types are used to store text. SQL offers several string types with varying length capabilities."},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Fixed-Length Strings"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"CHAR(n): Stores a fixed-length string of 'n' characters. If the stored string is shorter than 'n', it's padded with spaces. 'n' can range from 1 to 255 in some databases."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE states (
    state_code CHAR(2) PRIMARY KEY,
    state_name VARCHAR(50)
);"},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Variable-Length Strings"},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"VARCHAR(n): Stores a variable-length string of up to 'n' characters. It only uses the space needed to store the actual string. 'n' can range from 1 to a larger value (e.g., 65535 in MySQL)."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"TEXT: Stores large amounts of text. The maximum length varies by database system. Often used for storing articles, descriptions, etc."},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"MEDIUMTEXT: Stores medium-sized amounts of text, larger than TEXT but smaller than LONGTEXT (if supported by the database)."},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"LONGTEXT: Stores very large amounts of text. The maximum length is typically very large (e.g., 4GB in MySQL)."},{"order":32,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE articles (
    article_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    content TEXT
);"},{"order":33,"type":"heading","text":"Date/Time Data Types"},{"order":34,"type":"paragraph","text":"Date/Time data types are used to store dates and times. The specific types available and their behavior can vary significantly between database systems."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DATE: Stores a date (year, month, day). The format is typically YYYY-MM-DD."},{"order":36,"type":"bullet_point","text":"TIME: Stores a time (hour, minute, second). The format is typically HH:MM:SS."},{"order":37,"type":"bullet_point","text":"DATETIME or TIMESTAMP: Stores both date and time. DATETIME typically stores the date and time as is, while TIMESTAMP might be converted to UTC for storage and then back to the local time zone when retrieved. The exact behavior depends on the database system."},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"YEAR: Stores a year. Can be 2 digits or 4 digits depending on the database system."},{"order":39,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE events (
    event_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    event_date DATE,
    event_time TIME,
    event_datetime DATETIME
);"},{"order":40,"type":"paragraph","text":"It's important to consult the documentation for your specific database system (e.g., MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle) to understand the exact behavior and limitations of each data type, especially for Date/Time types."}]
